'''William Henry Andrews''' (born December 10, 1951) is an [[United States of America|American]] [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] and [[Biogerontology|biogerontologist]] whose career is centered on searching for a cure for human [[aging]]. Andrews is the founder and president of the [[biotechnology]] company [[Sierra Sciences]].<ref name="Rejuvenation">{{Citation | year =2011 | title = Personal Profile: Interview with Bill Andrews, Ph.D. | journal = [[Rejuvenation Research]] |url = http://www.liebertonline.com/doi/abs/10.1089/rej.2011.1237 | doi=10.1089/rej.2011.1237 | volume=14 | issue = 4 | pages=457–461| pmid = 21851179 | last1 = Andrews | first1 = B. | url-access = subscription }}</ref> In the 1990s, he led the team at [[Geron Corporation]] that was the first to successfully identify the genes for human enzyme telomerase.<ref name="Popsci">{{Citation | year = 2011 | title = The Man Who Would Stop Time | publisher = [[Popular Science]] |url = http://www.popsci.com/science/article/2011-07/man-who-would-stop-time}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | year = 1996 | title = Mammalian telomerase| publisher = United States Patent | url = https://patents.google.com/patent/US5583016}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | year = 1995 | title = The RNA component of human telomerase.| journal = [[Science (journal)|Science]] | pmid = 7544491 | doi=10.1126/science.7544491 | volume=269 | pages=1236–41 | last1 = Feng | first1 = J | last2 = Funk | first2 = WD | last3 = Wang | first3 = SS | issue = 5228| bibcode = 1995Sci...269.1236F| s2cid = 9440710|display-authors=etal}}</ref><ref name="2011 Patent">{{Citation | year = 2001 | title = Telomerase| publisher = United States Patent | url = https://patents.google.com/patent/US6261836}}</ref> This enzyme is responsible for preventing telomeres from shortening in human primordial germ cells (reproductive cells).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Zvereva|first1=M. I.|last2=Shcherbakova|first2=D. M.|last3=Dontsova|first3=O. A.|title=Telomerase: structure, functions, and activity regulation|journal=Biochemistry. Biokhimiia|year=2010 |volume=75|issue=13|pages=1563–1583|doi=10.1134/s0006297910130055|issn=1608-3040|pmid=21417995|s2cid=15987343 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Andrews was born on December 10, 1951, to television producer [[Ralph Andrews]] and Margaret Andrews. As a child, Andrews was told by his father that he should grow up to become a doctor and find a cure for aging.<ref name="Rejuvenation" /> Andrews graduated from [[Cate School]] in 1971. He graduated from the [[University of California, San Diego]] in 1976 with two [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degrees in Biology and Psychology, and earned his Ph.D. in Molecular and Population Genetics at the [[University of Georgia]] in 1981.<ref>{{Cite web|title=An Interview with Bill Andrews, Ph.D.|url=https://www.acimconnect.com/blog/Post/5618/An-Interview-with-Bill-Andrews-Ph-D|access-date=2021-07-14|website=ACIM Connect|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>[https://lifeboat.com/ex/bios.william.h.andrews Dr. William H. Andrews]</ref>

==Career==
Andrews has been a medical researcher in biotech since 1981.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Peters|first=Michael A.|date=2021-05-12|title=Against death. Longevity forever!|journal=Educational Philosophy and Theory|language=en|volume=53|issue=6|pages=559–562|doi=10.1080/00131857.2019.1684803|issn=0013-1857|doi-access=free}}</ref> He first worked at the [[biotechnology]] company Armos Corporation then Codon Corporation. Codon was purchased by Schering AG and became [[Bayer|Berlex Biosciences]]. In 1993, Andrews convinced Berlex to send him to an anti-aging conference at [[Lake Tahoe|Lake Tahoe, California]], where he met Calvin Harley of [[Geron Corporation]].<ref name="Rejuvenation" /> Harley gave a speech on the subject of [[Telomere|telomeres]] and [[telomerase]], their discovery in the organism [[Tetrahymena]] by [[Elizabeth Blackburn]] and [[Carol W. Greider|Carol Greider]], and on the possible connection between telomeres and aging. Harley mentioned that no one had yet been successful in discovering the genes for telomerase in human beings. After the speech, Andrews approached Harley and told him that he could discover the genes for human telomerase for Geron in three months. Harley hired Andrews as Geron's Director of Molecular Biology. Three and a half months later, Andrews' team cloned the RNA component of telomerase ("[[Telomerase RNA component|hTR]]").<ref name="Rejuvenation" /> For this discovery, and the demonstration that the anti-sense of hTR could kill every cancer cell tested, Andrews and 3 members of his team were awarded second place for "National Inventor of the Year" in 1997 by the [[Intellectual Property Owners Association]] (first place having been awarded for the invention of the HIV [[Protease inhibitor (biology)|Protease Inhibitor]]).<ref>{{Citation|title=Past Winners|url=http://www.ipo.org/AM/Template.cfm?Section=Home&Template=/CM/ContentDisplay.cfm&ContentID=7756|year=2005|publisher=Intellectual Property Organization}}</ref> Andrews' team later co-discovered the [[protein]] component of human telomerase ("[[Telomerase reverse transcriptase|hTERT]]") as well.<ref name="Rejuvenation" /><ref name="2011 Patent" />

In 1998, Andrews founded Yonder Technologies, that later became [[Sierra Sciences]] in 1999 in [[Reno, Nevada]], with the specific goal of curing human aging. Andrews assembled a team to search for a small molecule(s) that would bind to the telomerase [[Repressor|repressor(s)]], causing the body to constitutively express telomerase in the presence of that molecule(s).<ref name="Popsci" /> From 1999 to 2005, Sierra Sciences' focus was to identify the telomerase repressor protein, in the hopes that a drug could be specifically designed to bind to it. During this time frame, Geron Corporation discovered [[TA-65]], a small-molecule telomerase activator derived from [[Astragalus membranaceus]]. Sierra Sciences tested its efficacy,<ref>{{Citation | year = 2011 | title = A Natural Product Telomerase Activator As Part of a Health Maintenance Program | journal = [[Rejuvenation Research]] | doi=10.1089/rej.2010.1085 | volume=14 | pages=45–56 | pmid=20822369 | pmc=3045570 | last1 = Harley | first1 = CB | last2 = Liu | first2 = W | last3 = Blasco | first3 = M | issue = 1 |display-authors=etal}}</ref> and shortly thereafter, Andrews became the first paying customer to take the supplement.<ref name="Popsci" />

In 2005, Andrews switched to the "brute force" strategy of developing assays to screen large numbers of random chemicals to determine whether they induced expression of telomerase.<ref name="Rejuvenation" /> In November 2007, after nearly two years of screening, Sierra Sciences discovered the chemical C0056784,<ref name="Popsci" /> which induces approximately 5% as much telomerase as is found in the immortal cancer cell line [[HeLa]].<ref name="Achievements">{{Citation|title=Sierra Sciences: Achievements and Intellectual Property.|url=http://www.sierrasci.com/research/index.html|year=2011|publisher=[[Sierra Sciences]]}}</ref> In 2008, using C0057684 as a positive control, Sierra Sciences developed a more sensitive [[Real-time polymerase chain reaction|real-time PCR]] based [[high-throughput screening]] assay, the "hTERT RT-PCR assay," with which they were able to screen 4,000 chemicals per week.<ref name="Achievements" /> In 2010, Andrews and Sierra Sciences entered into an agreement with John Anderson, founder of [[Isagenix|Isagenix International]], to use the new assay to screen natural ingredients for telomerase activity. A year later, based on the assay's results, Isagenix launched Product B, a telomerase inducing nutraceutical.<ref>{{Citation|title=The Vision|url=http://www.stayoung.info/the-vision|year=2011|publisher=Stayoung.info}}</ref>

Andrews' team developed an hTERT Gene Therapy, using the Adeno-Associated Virus (AAV) as a vector, for research studies.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2012-11-01|title=Telomerase Therapies?|url=https://joshmitteldorf.scienceblog.com/telomerase-as-a-fountain-of-youth/|access-date=2021-07-14|website=Josh Mitteldorf|language=en-US}}</ref> This gene therapy was later licensed to Libella Gene Therapeutics in 2017 to be used in clinical studies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Science – Libella Gene Therapeutics|url=https://www.libellagenetherapeutics.com/science/|access-date=2021-07-14|language=en-US}}</ref> 

Andrews is a named inventor on over 50 US-issued patents on telomerase and author of numerous scientific research studies published in peer-reviewed scientific journals.<ref>{{Cite web|last=admin|title=Bill Andrews, Ph.D.|url=https://defytime.com/bill-andrews-ph-d/|access-date=2021-07-14|website=defytime®|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Andrews is an [[ultramarathon]] runner.<ref name="Popsci" /> In 2008<ref>{{Citation | year = 2008 | title = Badwater 2008 results | publisher = Ultra Signup | url = http://ultrasignup.com/results_event.aspx?did=3874}}</ref> and 2009,<ref>{{Citation | year = 2009 | title = 2009 Badwater Ultramarathon Results | publisher = AdventureCORPS | url = http://dbase.adventurecorps.com/results.php?bw_eid=49&bwr=Go}}</ref> he successfully completed the [[Badwater Ultramarathon]], a 135-mile race through [[Death Valley]] in temperatures approaching 130 °F (54 °C).<ref>{{cite web |last1=magazine |first1=Trail Runner |title="I want to Run a 7-Minute Mile When I'm 130" |url=https://www.trailrunnermag.com/people/qas-people/bill-andrews-ultrarunning-geneticist-curing-aging/ |website=[[Trail Runner Magazine]] |date=26 April 2017}}</ref>
